account:
It is day 1, about 07:14, and I am at the town hall with the secretary preparing for office at eight. I have read today's appointment book and the grain inspection brief. At ten I am due at the mill on the east bank to ask the miller about grain quantities, storage conditions, and supply concerns, and record findings and follow-up decisions. The brief is preparation only: I have not yet received stock figures or evidence of a grain problem. Later appointments are lunch at home at noon, council letters at thirteen hundred, tea with the neighbour at fifteen hundred, office at sixteen-thirty, and home at nineteen hundred.

One addition is Builder's request last night for an in-person inspection of completed great hall lighting at eighteen hundred today. I agreed and have just asked the secretary to add it to the book. This appears to be a review of the lighting work; I have not yet inspected it or established whether anything needs correcting.

The other unusual matter is a vague rumour the neighbour mentioned yesterday about a bridge or port change. The neighbour could not confirm it, and the secretary reported no actual proposal or correspondence substantiating it. I do not know whether any such change is planned or what it would be for, and should not treat the rumour as fact. I have just asked the secretary whether any new correspondence has arrived for this morning's office session; I am awaiting a response.
